questions.question: Select the term that will come next in the following series. M, E, P, H, S,?, V, N
questions.questionHtml:
Select the term that will come next in the following series.

M, E, P, H, S,?, V, N
questions.solution:
The given series is a combination of 2 series,

I) M, P, S, V

M + 3 = P;

P + 3 = S;

S + 3 = V;

II) E, H, ?, N

E + 3 =H;

H + 3 = K;

K + 3 = N;

Hence, “K” is the missing term in the given series.

questions.question: The sum of the current ages of Shipra and Malini is 65 years. After 5 years, Shipra’s age will be 15 years more than Malini’s age. What is Malini’s current age?
questions.questionHtml: The sum of the current ages of Shipra and Malini is 65 years. After 5 years, Shipra’s age will be 15 years more than Malini’s age. What is Malini’s current age?
questions.solution:
Let the age of Shipra be” x” and age of Malini be “y”.

As per statement given in question:

x + y = 65      ----(i) and

After 5 years,

Shipra = x + 5

Malini = y + 5

→ x + 5 = (y + 5) + 15

→ x = y + 15      ----(ii)

From both the equation (i) and (ii)

y + 15 + y = 65,

2y = 50,

y = 25,

and x = 40

Hence, Malini’s current age is “25 years”

questions.question: Two statements are given followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts. Decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All utensils are spoons. All bowls are spoons. Conclusions: I. No utensil is a bowl. II. Some utensils are bowls. III. No spoon is a utensil.
questions.questionHtml:
Two statements are given followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts. Decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

Statements:

All utensils are spoons.

All bowls are spoons.

Conclusions:

I. No utensil is a bowl.

II. Some utensils are bowls.

III. No spoon is a utensil.

options.text: Either conclusion I or II follows
options.html: Either conclusion I or II follows

questions.solution:
Statement I: All utensils are spoons

Statement II: All bowls are spoons

Conclusion I: No utensil is a bowl → False (It is possible but not definite)

Conclusion II: Some utensils are bowls → False (It is possible but not definite)

Conclusion III: No spoon is a utensil → False.

Here, Conclusion I and II makes complementary pairs.

Hence, “Either conclusion I or II follows” is the correct answer.

questions.question: ‘A +B’ means ‘A is the sister of B’ ‘A - B’ means ‘A is the daughter of B’ ‘A × B’ means ‘A is the brother of B’ ‘A B’ means ‘A is the husband of B’ IfV + U × Q – T + R + P × S, then how is P related to V?
questions.questionHtml:
‘A +B’ means ‘A is the sister of B’

‘A - B’ means ‘A is the daughter of B’

‘A × B’ means ‘A is the brother of B’

‘A B’ means ‘A is the husband of B’

IfV + U × Q – T + R + P × S, then how is P related to V?
questions.solution:
According to the question, V + U × Q – T + R + P × S can be decoded as V is sister of U, U is brother of Q, Q is daughter of T, T is sister of R, R is sister of P, P is brother of S.

Hence from the above arrangement, P is maternal uncle of V.

questions.question: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the following equation correct? 5 + 16 – 4 × 14 ÷ 2 = 59
questions.questionHtml:
Which two signs should be interchanged to make the following equation correct?

5 + 16 – 4 × 14 ÷ 2 = 59
questions.solution:
Given expression: - 5 + 16 – 4 × 14 ÷ 2 = 59

1) Interchanging ÷ and –

Equation will become :- - 5 + 16÷ 4 × 14 - 2

= 5 + 4 × 14 – 2

= 5 + 56 – 2

= 59

2) Interchanging × and +

Equation will become :- 5 × 16 – 4 + 14 ÷ 2

= 80 – 4 + 7

≠ 59

3) Interchanging + and –

Equation will become :- 5 - 16 + 4 × 14 ÷ 2

= 5 – 16 + 28

≠ 59

4) Interchanging ÷ and ×

Equation will become :- 5 + 16 – 4 ÷ 14 × 2

= 5 + 16 – 0.57

≠ 59

Thus, interchanging “÷ and -” we get the correct answer.

questions.question: Three different positions of the same dice are shown here. Which number is on the face opposite the face showing ‘5’?
questions.questionHtml: Three different positions of the same dice are shown here. Which number is on the face opposite the face showing ‘5’?
questions.solution:
The number 4 appears in 3 dice position i.e. 1st 2nd and 3rdfrom which it is evident that 6, 2, 1, 5 are adjacent to it and cannot be opposite to number 4. From this we can conclude that number 4 faces number 3.

Similarly Number 6 appears in 2 dice position i.e. 1st and 3rd from which it is evident that 2, 4 and 5 are adjacent to it and cannot be opposite to number 6. Also, number 4 faces number 3. From this we can conclude that number 6 faces number 1.

From the above conclusions we can say that Number 5 will be facing number 2.

Hence, “2” is the correct answer.

questions.question: Who among the following was the last Nawab of Awadh?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following was the last Nawab of Awadh?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Wajid Ali Shah.

Key Points

  • Wajid Ali Shah was the eleventh and last King of Awadh.
  • Lord Dalhousie, Governor General of British India, had deposed him under the pretext of misgovernance in February 1856.
  • Wajid Ali Shah's first wife was Alam Ara who was better known as Khas Mahal ( transl. special wife).
  • Begum Hazrat Mahal, also known as the Begum of Awadh, was the second wife of Nawab of Awadh Wajid Ali Shah.​

Additional Information

  •  About Awadh.
    • The ancient name of Awadh was  Kosala,
    • The Avadh is located in Uttar Pradesh.
    • Awadh city is located on the bank of the Gomti river.
    • Saadat Khan Burhanul Mulk is also known as the father of Awadh, established in 1722.
    • Faizabad was made the first capital of Awadh.
    • Wajid Ali Shah was the eleventh and last King of Awadh.

questions.question: Which state of India was ruled by the Ahom Dynasty?

questions.solution:

questions.question: Wind turbines convert ________ energy into mechanical power.
questions.questionHtml: Wind turbines convert ________ energy into mechanical power.
questions.solution:
• Wind turbines convert kinetic energy into mechanical power.
  • The kinetic energy is basically the energy of the moving wind.
  • This energy is imparted to the blades of the turbine.
  • The blades in turn, rotate a shaft which is connected to a generator that generates electricity.

questions.question: Which theory is used to make long-run predictions about exchange rates in a flexible exchange rate system?
questions.questionHtml: Which theory is used to make long-run predictions about exchange rates in a flexible exchange rate system?
questions.solution:
• The Purchasing Power Parity (PPP) Theory can make long term predictions about exchange rates in a flexible exchange rate system.
  • Basically PPP compares the economic productivity and standards of living of countries to predict exchange rates between different currencies.
  • A simple formula for PPP is S = (P1 / P2) where 
    • S is the exchange rate between two currencies 1 and 2
    • P1 is price of good X in country 1
    • P2 is price of good X in country 2 
  • For an accurate prediction a range of goods should be compared with the PPP theory.

questions.question: In which year was the Battle of Saragarhi fought?
questions.questionHtml: In which year was the Battle of Saragarhi fought?
questions.solution:

questions.solution:

  • The red blood cells are made from stem cells in the bone marrow.

questions.question: Which of the following is the largest container port of India?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is the largest container port of India?
questions.solution:
The Jawaharlal Nehru Port is the largest container port in India.

It is located in Navi Mumbai.

The port alone handles about 40% of the countries ocean cargo.

The port serves as the major cargo hub for Karnataka, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, and Maharashtra.

questions.question: Which theory in economics proposes that countries export what they can most efficiently and plentifully produce?
questions.questionHtml: Which theory in economics proposes that countries export what they can most efficiently and plentifully produce?
questions.solution:
• The Heckscher-Ohlin Model proposes that countries export what they can produce very efficiently and in high quantities.
  • It is also popularly known as the H-O Model or 2x2x2 model.
  • It is used to examine the trade equilibrium between two countries.
  • It takes into consideration that countries should ideally export materials and resources of which they have an excess, while proportionately importing those resources they need.

questions.question: Which was the wettest place in India in 2018 as per the India Meteorological Department (IMD)?

  • It received more rain (5,619 mm) than even Cherrapunji which was known to be the wettest place in the country for many years.
  • This was because Cherrapunji received significantly less rainfall (4730 mm) compared to previous years.

questions.question: Identify the part of brain that controls the maintenance of posture, balance and equilibrium.
questions.questionHtml: Identify the part of brain that controls the maintenance of posture, balance and equilibrium.
questions.solution:
The cerebellum is responsible for the maintenance of posture, balance and equilibrium.

It is located behind the top part of the brain stem (where the spinal cord meets the brain).

The cerebellum makes up about 10% of the brain's weight.

Despite that, it contains about half of all the brains neurons (special cells that transmit information between sensory organs and brain).

questions.question: Five cubes, each of edge 3 cm are joined end to end. What is the total surface area of the resulting cuboid, in cm 2 ?
questions.questionHtml: Five cubes, each of edge 3 cm are joined end to end. What is the total surface area of the resulting cuboid, in cm<sup>2</sup>?
questions.solution:
Side of each cube = 3 cm

Five cubes are joined end to end, then length of newly formed cuboid = 3 × 5 = 15 cm

Breadth of newly formed cuboid = 3 cm

Height of newly formed cuboid = 3 cm

As we know,

Total surface area of cuboid = 2 (lb + bh + hl)

⇒ 2 (15 × 3 + 3 × 3 + 3 × 15)

⇒ 2 (45 + 9 + 45)

⇒ 2 × 99

⇒ 198 cm2

questions.question: The price of sugar is increased by 17%. A person wants to increase his expenditure by 5% only. By approximately what percent should he decrease his consumption?
questions.questionHtml: The price of sugar is increased by 17%. A person wants to increase his expenditure by 5% only. By approximately what percent should he decrease his consumption?
questions.solution:
Let the initial price of sugar be 100x

Price of sugar after increased = 100x × [117 / 100] = 117x

Person wants his expenditure increase by 5% only, so his expenditure should be = 100x × [105 / 100] = 105x

Required percentage = [(117 – 105x) / 117] × 100 = 10.3% (approx)

questions.question: The value of 15.2 + 5.8 ÷ 2.9 × 2 - 3.5 × 2 ÷ 0.5 is equal to:
questions.questionHtml: The value of 15.2 + 5.8 ÷ 2.9 × 2 - 3.5 × 2 ÷ 0.5 is equal to:
questions.solution:
Follow BODMAS rule to solve this question, as per the order given below :

Step-1: Parts of an equation enclosed in 'Brackets' must be solved first, and in the bracket,

Step-2: Any mathematical 'Of' or 'Exponent' must be solved next,

Step-3: Next, the parts of the equation that contain 'Division' and 'Multiplication' are calculated,

Step-4: Last but not least, the parts of the equation that contain 'Addition' and 'Subtraction' should be calculated.      

⇒ 15.2 + 5.8 ÷ 2.9 × 2 - 3.5 × 2 ÷ 0.5

⇒ 15.2 + 2 × 2 – 3.5 × 4

⇒ 15.2 + 4 – 14

⇒ 19.2 – 14 = 5.2

questions.question: In a class of 50 students, 40% are girls. The average marks of the whole class are 64.4 and the average of the boy’s marks is 62. What is the average mark of the girls?
questions.questionHtml: In a class of 50 students, 40% are girls. The average marks of the whole class are 64.4 and the average of the boy’s marks is 62. What is the average mark of the girls?
questions.solution:
Total number of students in the class = 50

Number of girls in class = 50 × 40/100 = 20

Number of boys in class = 50 – 20 = 30

Average marks of whole class = 64.4

Sum of marks of whole class = 64.4 × 50 = 3220

Average marks of boys = 62

Sum of marks of boys = 62 × 30 = 1860

Sum of marks of girls = 3220 – 1860 = 1360

Average marks of girls = 1360/20 = 68

questions.question: In a circle of radius 17 cm, a chord is at a distance of 8 cm from the centre of the circle. What is the length of the chord?
questions.questionHtml: In a circle of radius 17 cm, a chord is at a distance of 8 cm from the centre of the circle. What is the length of the chord?
questions.solution:
Let AB is chord and point M is the midpoint of AB, O is the centre.

Given, OM = 8 cm and Radius OB = 17 cm

In ΔOMB

Using Pythagoras theorem

⇒ (OB)2 = (OM)2 + (MB)2

⇒ 172 = 82 + (MB)2

⇒ MB = √(289 – 64) = 15

As we know, AB = 2 MB

AB = 2 × 15 = 30 cm

questions.question: In a circle with centre O, an arc ABC subtends an angle of 110° at the centre of the circle. The chord AB is produced to a point P. Then ∠CBP is equal to:
questions.questionHtml: In a circle with centre O, an arc ABC subtends an angle of 110° at the centre of the circle. The chord AB is produced to a point P. Then ∠CBP is equal to:
questions.solution:
The angle subtended by an arc at the centre of a circle is double the size of the angle subtended by the same arc at the circle circumference

Take any point Q on the circumference and join AQ and QC .

∴ ∠AOC = 2 × ∠AQC

⇒ ∠AQC = 1/2 × ∠AOC = 1/2 × 110° = 55°

Now, ∠CBP = ∠AQC [exterior angle of cyclic quadrilateral]

⇒ ∠CBP = 55°

questions.question: In ΔABC, P is a point on BC such that BP : PC = 4 : 11. If Q is the midpoint of BP, then ar(ΔABQ) : ar(ABC) is equal to:
questions.questionHtml: In ΔABC, P is a point on BC such that BP : PC = 4 : 11. If Q is the midpoint of BP, then ar(ΔABQ) : ar(ABC) is equal to:
questions.solution:
Given, BP : PC = 4 : 11

Suppose BP = 4 unit and PC = 11 unit

questions.solution:

questions.question: If \(\sqrt x + \frac{1}{{\sqrt x }} = \sqrt 6 ,\) then \({x^2} + \frac{1}{{{x^2}}}\) is equal to:
questions.questionHtml: If \(\sqrt x + \frac{1}{{\sqrt x }} = \sqrt 6 ,\)then \({x^2} + \frac{1}{{{x^2}}}\) is equal to:
questions.solution:
As we know,

⇒ (x + 1/x)2 = x2 + 1/x2 + 2

Given, √x + 1/√x = √6

⇒ (√x + 1/√x)2 = (√x)2 + (1/√x)2 + 2

⇒ [√6]2 = x + 1/x + 2

⇒ x + 1/x = 6 - 2 = 4

⇒ (x + 1/x)2 = x2 + (1/x)2 + 2

⇒ 42 = x2 + 1/x2 + 2

⇒ x2 + 1/x2 = 16 – 2 = 14

questions.question: Walking at 7/9 of his usual speed, a person reaches his office 10 minutes later than the usual time. His usual time in minutes is:
questions.questionHtml: Walking at 7/9 of his usual speed, a person reaches his office 10 minutes later than the usual time. His usual time in minutes is:
questions.solution:
As we know,

Time is inversely proportional to speed.

Let the usual speed of the person be 9x

Speed of the person after decreasing = 7x

Ratio of usual speed to after decreasing = 9x : 7x

Ratio of usual time to after decreasing = 7x : 9x

9x – 7x = 10

⇒ x = 5

∴ 7x = 7 × 5 = 35 min

Alternate MethodLet the usual speed be 's' m/s, and the usual time taken is 't' min. Since the distance covered is the same in both cases, we can equate:

s × t =  7s/9 × (t + 10)

9t = 7t + 70

t = 35 min

questions.solution:
SP of each article = Rs. 962

CP of first article = 962 × [100/130] = 740

CP of second article = 962 × [100/74] = 1300

Total SP of both article = 962 × 2 = 1924

Total CP of both article = 740 + 1300 = 2040

Total Loss = 2040 – 1924 = 116

Loss percentage = [116/2040] × 100 = 5.7% (approx)

questions.question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word. PROGRESSIVE
questions.questionHtml:

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Conservative'.

Key Points

  • The word 'Progressive,' refers to the advocacy for or implementation of social reform or new liberal ideas. ("प्रगतिशील").
    • For example, "The leadership in the company is progressive, always looking for innovative ideas and solutions."
  • 'Conservative' refers to the holding of traditional attitudes and values and cautious about change or innovation. ("संविधानसंरक्षी").
    • For example, a conservative approach to a problem would be to stick with tried and true methods, rather than trying something new and innovative.

Therefore, the correct answer is 'option 3'.

Additional Information

  • 'Repeated' means something that occurs again either immediately or after a set period. ("दोहराया हुआ").
  • 'Moving' can refer to the act of moving from one place to another, or it can also mean causing strong feelings of sadness or sympathy. ("हिलने वाला" or "भावुक").
  • 'Aristocratic' refers to something that is characteristic of the aristocracy, or a class of people considered to be above the common people, often due to birth or descent. ("सर्वोच्च वर्ग से संबंधित").

Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct order.

A. He would sit at the edge of her mother's bed and stare into her crib.

B. Arvind bumbled down the interminable corridor, suddenly reminded of his daughter in the days after she was born.

C. As a proportion to the fragment of life his daughter had seen, an hour was a vast sprawling space.

D. Some days he would imagine the world through her eyes and he would feel in his heart how long an hour actually was.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is BADC.
Key Points:- 

  • First is B as it defines what Arvind is reminded of i.e his daughter.
  • Next is A as it describes how he would stare at her and options C and D give an account of what he felt.
  • After A it should be D as C clearly is followed by D because D mentions how long an hour was and C further explains that an hour was a vast sprawling space for his daughter.


Therefore, the correct sequence of the paragraph is BADC.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. I am quite satisfied that I have not been ________ in doing whatever was needful for building up their character.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

I am quite satisfied that I have not been ________ in doing whatever was needful for building up their character.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 4.

Key Points

  • Let's see the meanings of the given words-
    • Affectionate means readily feeling or showing fondness or tenderness.
    • Caring means displaying kindness and concern for others.
    • Devoted means very loving or loyal.
    • Negligent means failing to take proper care of something.
  • Negligent should be used to describe that she was satisfied that she did not fail in doing whatever was needful for building up their character.
